title: Traffic split, shadowing, and auto-rollback policy for model rollout routing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: We need a robust, configurable routing layer for model rollouts that supports canary ramps, A/B splits, shadowing without impacting latency SLOs, and deterministic auto-rollback when quality or latency regressions are detected. This ticket scopes the routing & fallback policy implementation: (1) model variant compatibility checks at routing time, (2) region-aware failover rules that respect customer tier and capacity reservations, (3) shadow traffic plumbing that samples requests to new variants for evaluation, and (4) an auto-rollback engine driven by configurable signal thresholds (latency, error-rate, quality metrics from evals).

Goals:
- Provide a declarative rollout policy DSL that operators (and the Console) can use to configure canaries, A/B splits, and shadowing.
- Ensure routing decisions are safe: only route to compatible model variants for the request signature (tokenizer/IO schema/version).
- Implement tiered capacity routing so dedicated customers stay on reserved pools while shared-hosted traffic can fallback to cheaper variants when capacity is constrained.
- Implement an auto-rollback controller with clear, auditable reasons for rollbacks and a fast path for manual abort.

Non-goals: full UI for rule authoring (Console work will follow), deep model evaluation harness (we'll integrate with existing evals infra).
tasks: Design rollout policy DSL + JSON schema (include canary ramp schedule, shadow sample rate, AB weights, compatibility constraints)
Add runtime compatibility checker (model IO/tokens/kv-schema) to routing path
Implement routing priority layers: customer-tier -> region affinity -> canary/A-B weights -> fallback variants
Build shadow path that emits copies to evaluation queue with bounded sampling to avoid KV cache blowup
Create auto-rollback controller (configurable thresholds for p95 latency, 5xx rate, eval-quality delta) and expose endpoints for status/events
Expose events and traces for rollouts to Console (work with observability team)
acceptance_criteria: New rollout policy can be submitted as JSON and validated against schema
Runtime rejects routing to incompatible model variants and surfaces clear error messages
Canary ramp can be scheduled: 1% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated waits and metric checks
Shadow traffic can be enabled at configurable sample rate without increasing tail latency by >5% on host path
Auto-rollback triggers when configured thresholds exceeded, with rollback executed within configured cool-down
Fallback to region-capable model variant happens automatically when region/node level capacity constrained for hosted customers, while dedicated customers remain on reserved pools
monitoring: Metrics to emit: rollout.active, rollout.canary_percentage, rollout.shadow_sample_rate, rollout.rollback_count, rollout.rollback_reason, routing.incompatible_count, routing.fallback_invocations, p95_latency_by_rollout, 5xx_rate_by_rollout, eval_quality_delta_by_rollout. Dashboards: rollout summary, per-model-variant health, region capacity heatmap. Alerts: p95 increases >30% vs baseline or 5xx rate >2% for 5m during a ramp (configurable).
rollback_policy: Default thresholds: p95 latency increase >25% over baseline OR 5xx rate >1.5% sustained for 3 minutes OR eval-quality drop >3% absolute. Auto-rollback respects a cool-down window (default 10 minutes) and requires an audit event with reason. Manual pause/abort must be available via Console and as an API call. Rollback will choose last known-good variant and ramp traffic back over a configurable period.
